intro.text: The glowing light held in gemstones on Roshar. Stormlight is the best known.
The glowing Investiture of Roshar's Shards, held in gemstones: Stormlight, Voidlight and Lifelight, and blends of them.

description.text: Stormlight glows inside gemstones, and Szeth draws it in to fuel his powers.
Roshar has three pure Lights, one from each of its Shards: Stormlight from Honor, Voidlight from Odium and Lifelight from Cultivation.

items.text: Stormlight glows white with a faint blue tint, and through a prism gives a rainbow with a wide blue band. Its rhythm is stately.
Voidlight came to Roshar only in Desolations, given by Odium to servants who sang the Song of Prayer. It leaks from gems far more slowly than Stormlight.
Rushu calls Voidlight's purple-on-black glow "hyperviolet". Its rhythm is chaotic, but with a certain logic to it.
Lifelight, Cultivation's Light, may be the rarest. Lift alone can make it, from food. It glows white with a faint green tint and helps plants grow even better than Stormlight.
Towerlight is the light of the Sibling, a blend of Honor's and Cultivation's Light. It glows a soft blue-green.

Towerlight's rhythm, the Rhythm of the Tower, joins Cultivation's growing energy with Honor's calm order. Through a prism it splits into two rainbows, one with a wider blue band and one with a wider green.
Only the Sibling and their Bondsmith can make Towerlight; it needs the Sibling to hear both Cultivation's song and Honor's, which Navani gives them.

Navani and Raboniel make Warlight, a blend of Stormlight and Voidlight, in a gem vibrating to the Rhythm of War, made from the harmony of their two songs. It seems to need both a human and a singer to make.
Warlight glows a vivid black-blue. In a gem it swings between swirling like a storm and falling calm, and its rhythm is a burst of chaotic notes held in by a steady pulse.
No Light blending Odium and Cultivation is known, but Venli tunes to a rhythm of those two Shards, so one probably exists.
A Light and its anti-Light destroy each other on contact, perhaps more violently under pressure, as inside a gemstone.
Anti-Light behaves much like ordinary Light, but must be made with Intent: the Light is cut off from its Shard's tone, in a vacuum, and drawn to a gem vibrating to the opposite tone.
To a human the song of anti-Voidlight sounds the same as Voidlight's, but to a Fused it is unbearable.
Gavilar Kholin obtained a sphere of anti-Voidlight before his death, and it leads Navani to work out how to make anti-Light.
Anti-Voidlight glows faintly violet-black and warps the air. Touched to the soul of a Fused or other being of Odium, it destroys the Voidlight there and kills them for good.
Raboniel then makes anti-Stormlight. It harms beings Invested by Honor as anti-Voidlight harms those of Odium, and with Raysium weapons it can kill Radiant spren, breaking their bonds.
Lights behave a little like light and a little like liquids and gases, but are none of these.
Through a prism, a Light makes an impossible rainbow, with one colour band far wider than the rest.
Light moved between gems by sound follows the sound, much as liquid flows through a siphon.
How long a gem holds Light depends on the Light and the gem. Gems dim slowly at first and then fast, and perfect gems are said to hold Light for ever.
Before the True Desolation, ways of moving Stormlight from gem to gem were closely kept secrets of artifabrians.
The Arnist Method drains Light from a small gem into several larger empty ones of the same kind.
The Vriztl Guild of Thaylenah moves Light with tuning forks: a gem made to vibrate to a Light's pure tone leads a line of Light from a full gem into an empty one.
Like the Shards it comes from, Light has Intent.
Each Light vibrates to the pure tone of its Shard and to that Shard's rhythm; together they are called the Shard's song.
Singing or playing a Light's tone and rhythm can draw it in. Raboniel thinks Light answers to sound because it recalls its Shard's voice.
Each pure tone has an opposite, made with Intent, which pushes its Light away instead of drawing it.
Odium's tone and its opposite sound the same to a human, but to a Fused the opposite is deeply unpleasant.
